lines.text: Hello? Can anyone hear me? I think I'm on mute. No, I'm not on mute. Hang on.
I can hear you, Daniel. You're a bit quiet, though.
Quiet. Okay, let me move this microphone thing. Is that better?
Much better, yes. Now you're loud.
Ha. Great. Goldilocks audio, I'll take it.
Morning, everyone. Sorry, I'm still getting my camera to come on. It says it's in use by another application.
Is that the one where you have to close the other call first?
Probably. I thought I'd closed everything. Give me a second, I'll just leave it off if it doesn't work.
Morning all. Can you see my screen, or is it just my face? I'm trying to share the tracker but it's being slow.
I just see your face. Nice and clear, though.
Thanks, I think. Okay, give it a moment. It's loading. There, now it should be up.
Yes, I can see the tracker now. It's a bit small. Can you zoom in?
Is that better? Let me make it bigger. Oh, that's too big. Hang on.
That's fine, that's readable. Leave it there.
Okay, camera's on. Or is it? Can you see me?
We see a very dark rectangle. Is that you?
Yeah, that's me. The light's behind me, I'll turn around. Better?
Yes, there you are. Hello, Marcus.
Hello. Sorry, long morning already and it's not even properly started.
Mm-hm, same here. I had a bit of a fight with the lift this morning, and then the coffee machine.
The coffee machine is always the real problem.
It is. Whoever designed it clearly never needed a coffee at this time of day.
Ha. Right.
It's properly cold today, isn't it? I came in with my coat and gloves and I still wasn't warm.
Same. I'm sitting here with a scarf on. You can't see it, but I'm wearing a scarf.
I can see it, Daniel. It's a nice scarf.
Thank you. It's the only thing keeping me going.
Okay, I think everyone's here, so let's get going. Updates on the movers, Radix and the X-ray, the licence, and the handover date.
Sounds good. Are we going in that order?
Yes, that order. Movers first, then Radix, and we'll see how far we get on the others.
Okay, fine by me.
Marcus, the revised movers quote?
Yes. So I've got it open here. Give me one second, I just want to get the right line up so I don't misquote it.
Take your time.
Okay. Right. The revised quote with the weekday split is thirty three thousand, so we're three thousand over budget now instead of twelve.
Sorry, say that again? Thirty three thousand, and over by three? Or did I mishear?
Thirty three thousand is the quote. Over budget by three thousand. It was twelve over before.
Right, right. So that's quite a big move from the first one.
It is, yeah. That's what the weekday split did.
Can I just check, the thirty three, is that the whole thing? Or is that one part of it?
That's the number on the revised quote. That's what I've got in front of me, thirty three thousand.
Okay. I just wanted to be sure we were talking about the same figure.
And the budget figure that three is measured against, that's the same one we've been using the whole time? Not something that got changed?
Same one. The twelve over was against that, and the three over is against that. Nothing's changed on the budget side.
Okay. I just wanted to make sure we weren't comparing two different things.
No, that makes sense to check.
Mm-hm. I did check it twice myself, to be fair. I didn't believe it the first time.
Ha, I can understand that. Twelve down to three is quite a difference.
It is. I'd have liked to say it was my negotiating, but really it's the quote that changed.
Well, you asked for it to be revised, so some credit.
I'll take a bit of credit, thanks.
Okay. Let me just think about this for a second. Three thousand over.
Is that something contingency can absorb? I don't remember what we said about that.
Three thousand we can take from contingency. So the budget issue is basically resolved.
Okay. Good. That's what I was hoping you'd say, to be honest.
Basically resolved. Is there a part that isn't resolved? You said basically.
No, I just mean the budget side is sorted. It's a figure of speech, Siti. I'm not hiding anything.
Okay, I just wanted to hear it. Sorry, I'm picking at words.
No, it's fine, it's good to ask.
I suppose I'd just say, going back to what you said earlier, Marcus, it's still over. It's just over by a smaller amount.
Yes, still over. Three thousand over, and that's what we'd be covering from contingency.
Right. I'm not objecting. I just like to say it out loud so it's in the room.
Fair. It is still over, and we're covering it. Both of those are true.
Yeah. That's all I wanted.
Do you want me to say anything more about the weekday split? Or are people happy with that?
I'm curious, honestly. What does the weekday split actually mean in the quote? I'm only seeing the headline figure.
It's in the revised quote, that's the version we've been talking about. I don't want to go into details I haven't got in front of me. The headline is the thirty three.
Fair enough. I just wondered. I'm happy with the headline.
Yeah, me too. Nothing on my side.
Okay. Anything else on the quote before I say something? Anyone?
Not from me.
No. Go ahead.
Let's accept the revised quote at thirty three thousand.
Okay. Good. Right.
Fine by me.
Yes, agreed.
Good, that's one off the list. That was the one I was dreading a bit, if I'm honest.
Why dreading? It came in better than before.
I know, I know. I just didn't want to be the one to bring a number and then have it all go round again.
No, it was clear. Thank you, Marcus.
Thanks.
Sorry, one more thing, I just want to be sure I've got the numbers right in my notes. Thirty three thousand, three over, twelve before. Is that right?
That's right. Thirty three, three over, twelve before.
Good. Okay. I've got that.
Right, Siti, any news from Radix?
Yes, there's some. Hold on, let me find my notes. I had them open a minute ago.
Take your time. We'll just admire Marcus's dark rectangle.
It's not dark now, it's fixed.
It's a lot better, yes. I can see your face.
Okay, found it. Sorry. So, Radix confirmed one engineer slot on the eleventh of February, and the second provisional date fell through.
The second one fell through. Right. So we're down to the one.
We're down to the one, yes.
Sorry, just to be clear, the eleventh of February is the one that's confirmed? Not the provisional?
The eleventh is the confirmed one. The provisional was the second date, and that's the one that fell through.
Okay, got it. I got a bit tangled.
No, it's confusing. There were two dates floating around and now there's one.
The eleventh of February. Okay. I'll write that down so I don't lose it.
Mm-hm. And that's one engineer. Just the one.
One engineer, one slot, yes.
Right. Okay.
So we have a slot before cutover, but with no backup, if that engineer is sick we're stuck.
Yeah. That's the thing that's slightly uncomfortable. If it's one person on one day.
That's what I'm saying. There's nothing behind it.
But it is before cutover. That part's good.
Yes, that part's good. It's before cutover. I don't want to sound too negative.
No, you're not. You're describing it. It's good and it's thin, both.
Yes, exactly that. Good and thin.
Ha, that could go on a t-shirt.
Good and thin. Right.
I did ask about the second date. They just said it didn't work out, and that's all I've got on it.
Okay. So nothing more to be said about why.
No, nothing more. I don't know any more than that.
Fair enough.
And the eleventh, that's a firm slot as far as they've said? Not tentative?
They confirmed it. That's the word they used, confirmed.
Okay. Good. I just wanted to hear that word.
Yes. Confirmed.
Better than last week. Can we get their written confirmation?
Yes, they're sending it today.
Today. Okay, that's quick.
That's good. Today's good.
Yes. Good. I feel a bit better about that than I did a week ago, anyway.
Yes, me too. A week ago I had nothing to tell you, so even a single slot is something.
It's progress. It's not perfect, but it's progress.
Mm-hm. I'd take that.
Sorry, I keep going back to it, but the no-backup thing, we're all comfortable just noting that for now? I'm not asking for anything, I just want to make sure it's been said properly.
It's been said. Siti said it clearly, one slot, no backup.
Yes, I said it. I wasn't trying to bury it.
No, no, I didn't think you were. Okay, I'm happy it's been said.
Fine. Moving on, then?
Yes. Let me just scroll the tracker down. Give me a second, it's gone slow again.
It's fine. Take your time.
Oh, mine's frozen too. Is it the connection or just the tracker?
It's moving again for me now. Can you see the next item?
Yes, it's back. I can see it.
Yep, fine here.
Good. Okay, the licence is next.
Licence.
We filed the licence transfer on Monday. The ministry now says processing is eight weeks, not six.
Sorry, say that again? Eight, not six?
Yes. Eight weeks. When we looked before, the figure we had was six.
Right. Okay. So it's two weeks longer than we were working with.
Two weeks longer, yes. That's the change.
Is that in writing from them, or is it what somebody said on the phone?
It's what the ministry told us when we filed. That's the figure we've been given, so that's the one I'm using.
Mm-hm. Okay. I just wanted to know which kind of figure it was.
Fair question. I'd say it's the one they're giving everybody now.
Eight weeks from Monday the seventh is early February. That's tight against the cutover.
Let me just count it forward. Monday the seventh, eight weeks on... yeah, I get early February as well.
Same here. I did it twice on the calendar because I didn't believe it the first time.
And the cutover is the thirteenth, so we're not far off it.
Yes, it still lands before the thirteenth, but there's no room left.
No room left. Okay. I want to be sure I'm hearing that properly. It does land before the thirteenth?
It does. Before the thirteenth. It just doesn't have any slack in it.
So if it were six weeks we'd have had some breathing space, and now we've used it.
That's a fair way to put it. The two extra weeks took it.
Hang on, so is the thirteenth the day we move, or the day everything has to be ready before?
The cutover. That's the date we've all been calling the cutover. I'm just saying the licence has to be through before it.
Right, right. I just wanted to say it out loud so we're all talking about the same thing.
Yeah, that helps me too, honestly. I sometimes lose track of which date is which.
No, that's useful. The licence lands before the thirteenth. That's what we have.
That's what we have. I'm not saying more than that, because I don't know more than that.
Can I ask, and I might be asking something obvious, does the eight weeks start from the day we filed, or from some other point?
From the filing. Monday. That's how Priya counted it too.
Okay. Good. That's what I assumed, I just wanted it said.
Mm-hm. And we're not hearing anything different from the ministry about that?
Not that I've been told. Eight weeks from filing. That's all I've got.
It's a bit annoying, though, isn't it. Six to eight, and just when we'd settled on the plan.
It is annoying. But it's still inside the date, so I'd rather say that part clearly as well.
No, sure, sure. I'm not arguing with it. I'm just saying it's annoying.
I think it's fine to say it's annoying. It's also still before the thirteenth. Both are true.
Both are true. Yes. Tight, but still before.
And I'd rather we all say it the same way, so nobody walks away thinking it's comfortable.
Agreed. It's not comfortable. It's early February, and the cutover is the thirteenth.
Wait, sorry, one more. When you said the ministry now says eight weeks, was that when you filed on Monday, or did it change after?
When we filed. We filed on Monday and that's when they gave us eight weeks.
Okay, so it wasn't a second message later. Good. That's clearer.
So the answer was already eight when you got it. Not six that moved to eight.
Well, we'd been expecting six. They said eight. So from our side it moved, but nobody changed their mind on us, if that makes sense.
Yeah. That makes sense. Okay.
Fine. I think we've got the licence as clearly as we can for now. Anything else on it before we move on?
Not from me. I just wanted to be sure I'd got the numbers right.
Nothing more from me. Eight weeks, early February, before the thirteenth, no room left.
Mm-hm. That's four things and I've got all four.
Good. Right. Let's go on.
Handover date in writing?
The landlord confirmed in writing, but the handover is now the twenty second of January, a week later than they said.
Oh. A week later than they said. Okay.
Hold on. So it's in writing. That part is good.
Yes, it's in writing. The date's just not the one we wanted.
Sorry, the twenty second of January. Is that the day we get the keys, or the day the building is finished?
It's the handover. That's the word they used. The building's handed over to us on the twenty second.
Okay. Handover. I'll stick with that word then.
And before it was a week earlier, you said.
A week earlier, yes. That's what they'd told us before. Now it's a week later than that.
Right. So the same thing, just pushed by a week.
Same thing, pushed by a week.
So the treatment rooms start a week later. Do we still make it?
That's what I was about to ask. Because I'd been thinking about the treatment rooms the whole time you were talking.
Yeah. It's the same worry I had when I read it.
And you said it's confirmed. So there's no chance of it moving again, or is that me being nervous?
I can only say what the letter says. It says the twenty second. I haven't got anything that says otherwise.
No, that's fair. I'm not asking you to promise. I'm just thinking aloud.
Sure. And I'd be thinking the same thing in your seat.
Can I check something? The treatment rooms start a week later because the handover is a week later. Is it a straight one for one?
That's how I read it. The handover moved by a week, so the start moves by a week.
Okay. Good. I just didn't want to assume.
So the question is still the one Priya asked. Do we make it?
Yes. Marcus, do we?
Just about, if the fit-out crew works two Saturdays. I'll check with them.
Just about. Okay. That's not a no.
It's not a no. It's also not a comfortable yes.
Right. So it depends on the two Saturdays.
It depends on the two Saturdays, yes. That's the condition I put on it.
Two Saturdays. Not more than two?
Two. That's what I said. I haven't got another number.
Okay. I only asked because it's easy to hear it differently.
No, that's fine. Two Saturdays.
And you'll check with the crew. Is it a question of whether they can, or whether they will?
Honestly, I don't know yet. That's why I said I'd check. I'd be guessing if I answered.
Okay. That's honest. I'd rather you say you don't know.
Yes, same. I'd rather have 'I'll check' than a confident answer that turns out to be wrong.
Well, I'm not going to pretend to be confident. Just about is the honest answer.
It sort of mirrors the licence, doesn't it. Just about, not much room.
It does. Both of them land, but neither has any slack.
That's a bit uncomfortable when you put it like that.
It is. But I'd still rather put it like that than pretend it isn't so.
No, agreed. Better to say it.
Mm-hm.
Sorry, going back to the handover for a second. The landlord said it in writing. Did they give a reason for the week?
Not that I've got in front of me. The letter gives the date. That's the part I have.
Okay. I just wondered. It doesn't change the date either way.
No. The date's the date. The twenty second.
The twenty second of January. I'm writing it down so I don't mix it up with anything else.
Good idea. And the licence is eight weeks from the seventh, early February.
Yes. Got both.
Can I ask something back at the licence, since we're comparing the two?
Go on.
Daniel, you said it lands before the thirteenth. Is that the same thirteenth Priya meant when she said cutover?
Yes. The same one. Before the thirteenth, and the thirteenth is the cutover.
Okay. Thanks. I just wanted to be certain I wasn't mixing two dates.
You're not. It's the one date.
Right. So let me say where we are, and you tell me if I've got any of it wrong.
The licence is eight weeks from Monday the seventh. That's early February. It lands before the thirteenth, but with no room left.
Yes. That's right.
And the handover is confirmed in writing for the twenty second of January, a week later than they'd said.
Yes, that's right.
And the treatment rooms start a week later, and we make it just about, if the fit-out crew works two Saturdays.
Just about, yes. And I'll check with them.
That's the same as I've got.
Same as mine.
Good. Does anyone think I've said something that doesn't match what we heard?
No. I think it's all the same as what was said.
No, it matches.
It matches.
Can I say one more thing, and it's not new, it's just me thinking?
Of course.
It's odd that both things came in this week and both of them are about a bit less time. I'm not saying anything is wrong. It just felt like a lot at once.
Yes, it did feel like a lot at once. I had the same feeling.
It's a coincidence, I'd say. They're two separate things, one's the ministry and one's the landlord.
Yeah, no, I know. They're separate. I just noticed it.
They're separate. Different people, different letters.
Right. Fine. I'll leave it there.
No, I'm glad you said it. It's easier to say it than to carry it quietly.
Thanks. Yes.
I'd add that the licence part still works. I don't want it to come across as worse than it is.
No, understood. It works. It's tight, but it works.
And mine, I'd say the same. It works just about.
Yes. Just about. That's the wording we keep.
I'm happy with that wording.
Me too.
Okay. Yes. Fine by me.
Okay. I think that's both topics covered for this stretch. Does anyone have anything else on either of them before we wrap?
Not on the licence. Not on the handover either. I'm clear on both.
Nothing from me.
Nothing, except that I'll check with the fit-out crew, like I said.
Yes. Thanks, Marcus. So to wrap up, the licence is eight weeks and still before the thirteenth, the handover is the twenty second of January, and you're checking with the crew.
That's it. Yes.
Good. Thanks, everybody. That was useful.
Thanks, Priya. Thanks, all.
Thanks. Bye, everyone.
Bye, all.
Bye, everyone.
